skill.name: code-reviewer
skill.description: Code review guidance for pull requests, quality checks, coding standards, and report drafting. Includes reference checklists and simple Python scripts for path validation and JSON report output.
skill.summary: Review code changes with checklists, standards, and simple report tooling.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static shell execution alerts are false positives caused by Markdown command fences and inline file references. The three Python scripts do allow JSON output to an arbitrary path, so the remaining confirmed risk is a scoped filesystem write issue.

remediation.issue: User controlled output file paths in Python scripts
remediation.suggestion: Restrict --output to project-relative paths, refuse overwrites unless a force flag is provided, and display the resolved path before writing.
Label install, container, deployment, and environment setup commands as examples that require explicit user approval before execution.

remediation.issue: Placeholder analysis can overstate review coverage
remediation.suggestion: Document that the scripts currently produce empty findings by default until real static analysis checks are implemented.

content.user_title: Review Code Changes With Structured Checklists
content.value_statement: Code reviews can miss quality, security, and maintainability issues. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured review workflow with checklists, standards, and report tooling.
actual_capabilities: Guides pull request reviews with quality, test, performance, security, and maintainability checks.
Provides reference files for review checklists, coding standards, and common anti-pattern categories.
Includes three Python command-line scripts that validate target paths and print review report summaries.
Supports optional JSON output to standard output or to a user-selected output file.
Lists common development commands for local checks, builds, tests, containers, and deployment examples.
limitations: The bundled Python scripts contain placeholder analysis and return empty findings by default.
The skill does not connect to GitHub or inspect pull request diffs automatically.
Command examples need project-specific review before an agent runs them.
It does not replace manual security review for sensitive systems.

use_cases.title: Prepare Pull Request Feedback
use_cases.description: Review a branch before merging and collect focused feedback on correctness, tests, security, and maintainability.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Reviews
use_cases.description: Use shared checklist prompts to make review comments more consistent across repositories and reviewers.

use_cases.title: Draft Review Reports
use_cases.description: Run the simple report scripts and turn their output into a readable review summary for a developer.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Small Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review for a focused change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the code-reviewer skill to review this change for readability, tests, and obvious bugs. Return prioritized findings with file references when available.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pull request using the checklist, coding standards, and common anti-pattern references. Group findings by correctness, security, performance, and maintainability.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Review Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured report generation after local checks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the available review scripts only after confirming safe commands. Summarize the results, note any empty or placeholder outputs, and list manual checks still required.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Release Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for a high-impact release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a release-focused review that checks risky changes, missing tests, security assumptions, performance risks, deployment commands, and rollback concerns. Separate blockers from advisory feedback.

output_examples.input: Review a feature branch before opening a pull request.
output: A prioritized review with correctness, tests, security, and maintainability sections.
A short list of blocking issues and advisory improvements.
Clear notes when the scripts return placeholder or empty findings.

output_examples.input: Generate a summary after running the review report generator.
output_examples.output: A concise report summary that lists status, target, finding count, and recommended follow-up checks.

output_examples.input: Create a team review checklist for a service change.
output_examples.output: A practical checklist covering code organization, tests, security controls, performance risks, and deployment readiness.

best_practices: Confirm each command before running it, especially install, container, and deployment commands.
Treat script output as a starting point because the bundled analysis is mostly placeholder logic.
Ask for the diff, test results, and project context before issuing final review conclusions.
anti_patterns: Do not present the placeholder scripts as a complete static analysis system.
Do not run deployment or environment setup commands without explicit user approval.
Do not give broad approval when important files, tests, or requirements were not inspected.

faq.question: Does this skill perform real static analysis?
faq.answer: Only limited analysis is implemented. The scripts validate paths and produce simple summaries with empty findings by default.

faq.question: Can it review pull requests automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide review work, but it does not connect to pull request APIs or fetch diffs on its own.

faq.question: Which languages does it target?
faq.answer: The skill describes review support for TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Swift, Kotlin, and Go.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use the scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. An assistant can run the Python scripts after confirming the command, target path, and output location.

faq.question: Is it safe to run every command in the guide?
faq.answer: No. Install, container, deployment, and environment commands should be reviewed and approved for each project first.

faq.question: What is the best use of this skill?
faq.answer: Use it to structure human review, prepare feedback, and identify areas that need deeper manual or tool-based inspection.
